items.title: Braves thinking about pitching in postseason; Astros working to get there
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: When Atlanta right-handers Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias combined for six strikeouts over the final three innings of a 6-2 victory against the Houston Astros on Friday -- a win that secured the Braves' eighth postseason appearance over the past nine seasons -- the effort exemplified the effectiveness of Atlanta's bullpen.
items.body:
When Atlanta right-handers Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias combined for six strikeouts over the final three innings of a 6-2 victory against the Houston Astros on Friday -- a win that secured the Braves' eighth postseason appearance over the past nine seasons -- the effort exemplified the effectiveness of Atlanta's bullpen.
Heading into their game Saturday night in Houston, the Braves (90-64) said they might soon welcome back another part of their stellar relief corps. Right-hander Robert Suarez (4-0, 0.56 ERA in 31 appearances) is expected to make a rehab outing for Triple-A Gwinnett on Sunday and could rejoin the Braves' active roster sometime after that.
Suarez, a ballyhooed free-agent signing last offseason, has been sidelined since June with right elbow inflammation.
"It's possible," Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Suarez's return. "Again, it's just re-evaluating him every day. Things have gone well. They've progressed well all throughout this rehab, so I don't anticipate anything. You just never know. It'd be nice to be able to see him in a big-league game, but I'm not sure if that's going to happen or not.
"There's a chance (Suarez returns for the postseason). As we sit here (Friday), I don't know how that's going to unfold. All the options are possible."
With the Braves (90-64) wrapping up a playoff berth on Friday, Weiss has the luxury of trying to map out a pitching plan for the postseason. Astros manager Joe Espada has no such advantage, as his team is 77-77 and still battling for a playoff spot, tied with the Texas Rangers (77-77) for the lead in the American League West.
Houston holds the tiebreaker over Texas.
The Astros are scheduled to face right-hander Grant Holmes (9-5, 3.49 ERA), the Saturday starter for Atlanta. He has no decisions in three starts this month, allowing two earned runs on eight hits and four walks with seven strikeouts across 13 innings. Holmes won three of five starts in August, including two scoreless outings against the Miami Marlins and Chicago White Sox.
Holmes will make his first career appearance against the Astros. He is 7-4 with a 3.24 ERA across 23 career interleague appearances (17 starts).
Right-hander Hayden Wesneski (5-2, 3.70 ERA) will start for the Astros on Saturday. He allowed a season-high seven runs (three earned) while working a season-low three innings in a 14-4 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday. He has given up four runs over his previous four starts combined, going 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA.
Wesneski is 0-2 with a 3.27 ERA in five career relief appearances against the Braves.
The Braves neutralized Astros slugger and American League MVP front-runner Yordan Alvarez on Friday. He finished 1-for-2 with a double, a run and two walks, with only one of his four plate appearances coming with a teammate on base.
Astros leadoff hitter Jeremy Pena finished 0-for-4 with two strikeouts while batting ahead of Alvarez and coming off three multi-hit games against the Kansas City Royals this week. Pena struck out to end the third and fifth innings, leaving Alvarez to lead off in the fourth and sixth.
Meanwhile, Daulton Varsho, Christian Walker and Taylor Trammell finished a combined 0-for-12 with seven strikeouts occupying the fifth, sixth and seventh spots in the Houston batting order.
"We're trying," manager Joe Espada said. "These guys are working their tails off to really try to put some good at-bats together. (Friday) wasn't the case."
--Field Level Media

items.title: UEFA defends draw policy after Ireland request, Israel dismisses FAI comments
items.author: Tommy Lund
items.creator: Tommy Lund
items.summary: Ireland's soccer association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel was rejected.
items.body:
UEFA said on Saturday that decisions on whether national teams should be kept apart in competition draws were made on a case-by-case basis and guided primarily by security considerations, after Ireland's soccer association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel had been rejected.
Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell said on Friday the body had asked UEFA if the Republic of Ireland and Israel could be separated in future draws after the teams were paired in February's Nations League draw.
The two sides are due to meet on September 27 and October 4 in the competition.
UEFA, European soccer's governing body, said requests to stop teams being drawn against each other were considered individually.
"Decisions to avoid certain teams being drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security," UEFA said a statement.
"UEFA handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments."
Courell told reporters the FAI had been informed that such an arrangement would not be possible because Ireland and Israel had "never been in direct conflict".
The Israel Football Association also responded to Courell's remarks, questioning whether a formal request had been made to UEFA.
"The question should be directed at UEFA: was there an official inquiry or request regarding this matter, or is this merely another inconsequential statement?" IFA head of communications Shlomi Barzel told Reuters.
"Since we long ago stopped getting worked up over statements detached from reality, we are focusing on high-quality professional preparations to achieve our goals on the pitch."
The fixtures have been controversial in Ireland amid the conflict in the Middle East.
Last November, members of the FAI [USN:L1N3WK056 TEXT:"voted overwhelmingly"] for its board to request that UEFA should suspend the IFA from European competitions, while in May leading Irish footballers and celebrities joined in a [USN:L4N41K064 TEXT:"campaign for a boycott"] of Ireland's home Nations League fixture.
[USN:L8N42G1NS TEXT:"Ireland's designated home"] match on October 4 is due to be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia, instead of Dublin, while Irish fans will not receive tickets for Israel's designated home fixture in Debrecen, Hungary, the previous weekend.

items.title: Fresh off rout, Nationals look to finish strong vs. Cards
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: After enduring Tommy John surgery and the subsequent monotonous rehab, Cade Cavalli said he wants to help make the Washington Nationals winners again.
items.body:
After enduring Tommy John surgery and the subsequent monotonous rehab, Cade Cavalli said he wants to help make the Washington Nationals winners again.
On the same day he signed a four-year, $47 million contract extension, Cavalli dominated for five scoreless innings against the St. Louis Cardinals and reached 200 strikeouts for the season in Washington's 9-1 victory on Friday.
It's safe to say anyone on the Nationals (72-82) will have a hard time topping those achievements when the series continues Saturday night in St. Louis. But Cavalli said the Nationals have been playing for each other all season.
"We're trying to finish on a really strong note," Cavalli said. "It's a really special opportunity to be in the big leagues every day, and you've got to treat it that way."
Cavalli, 28, continued his amazing first full season in the majors after making just one appearance with the Nats in 2022 before needing surgery. He allowed four hits and fanned six, giving him exactly 200 strikeouts in 32 starts. His last pitch was a changeup that fooled rookie JJ Wetherholt into watching it go by for strike three.
"When I was going through Tommy John after touching the big leagues for one game, I felt it in my heart and soul that I wanted to get back here and compete and be one of the best in the game," Cavalli said. "I truly believed in myself and the people around me really believed. I didn't get here by myself.
"It really settles in your heart that it's a special day."
Cavalli's extension buys out his three remaining arbitration years as well as his first year of free agency. The base value could become $70 million if a team option for 2031 is exercised.
The Nationals won the World Series in 2019, drafted Cavalli 22nd overall a year later, and have changed just about everything else since. The Juan Soto trade helped to replenish the organization, and under new manager Blake Butera this season, the team has shown signs of being competitive again.
"We're doing it as a group," Cavalli said. "We've got a good culture that we've already established, so there's no overhaul that needs to happen."
Left-hander Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.35 ERA) is scheduled to make his 16th start of the season on Saturday. He tossed seven shutout innings in his previous appearance against the Los Angeles Angels a week ago and has posted a 2.44 ERA in eight starts since Aug. 3.
Alvarez has yet to face the Cardinals in his career.
The Cardinals (75-79) were eliminated from wild-card contention with their third straight loss in the opener and are trying to avoid finishing under .500 for the third time in four seasons. But manager Oliver Marmol sees reasons for hope.
"Our guys committed to a certain style of play that they held each other accountable to every day," Marmol said. "They lived up to it really, really well."
Right-hander Michael McGreevy (7-9, 3.83) is scheduled to start Saturday's game. He has won three straight decisions and beat the Nationals in his lone career encounter in April, allowing a run and four hits over six innings.
--Field Level Media

items.title: India’s Silicon Valley Is Straining Under Its Own Growth
items.summary: Bangalore helped turn India into a global hub for software services, tech talent and outsourcing, building an ecosystem that now supports multinational firms, domestic startups and capital. But the city’s success has also become one of its biggest weaknesses. India still lacks the depth of capital available in the US and China, while Bangalore’s physical infrastructure has struggled to keep pace with private-sector growth. At the same time, southern India’s rising economic power is colliding with demographic and political shifts that could threaten its representation in the country’s Central Government, which helps support the growth that cities like Bangalore have enjoyed. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: UN peacekeeping chief in Lebanon says smooth transition is critical before pull-out
items.author: Maya Gebeily
items.creator: Maya Gebeily
items.summary: The head of United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon said on Saturday it was critical to ensure other UN agencies and Lebanese troops could assume the tasks carried out by the force before it begins withdrawing at the end of this year.
items.body:
The head of United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon said on Saturday it was critical to ensure other UN agencies and Lebanese troops could assume the tasks carried out by the force before it begins withdrawing at the end of this year.
Major General Diodato Abagnara of Italy spoke to Reuters in southern Lebanon at a position operated by the UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL, which has been monitoring hostilities in southern Lebanon for nearly 50 years.
Since a new war erupted between Israel and Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah in March, the force has also provided security escorts for humanitarian aid convoys to residents in a [USN:L6N40K0QV TEXT:"small cluster"] of predominantly Christian southern Lebanese towns now encircled by Israeli troops. Residents in much of the rest of southern Lebanon have been forcibly displaced by Israeli strikes and evacuation orders.
The UN Security Council has ordered UNIFIL to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026, [USN:L6N45502W TEXT:"triggering concerns"] over whether aid deliveries can continue and how the force can transfer its positions to Lebanese troops.
“There are other United Nations entities here in the south, and so what is very important for us (is) to conduct a very smooth transition to different entities, or for the future of a new mission,” Abagnara told Reuters.
He said UNIFIL was already working with the UN’s country team to ensure humanitarian assistance in Israeli-occupied areas and information sharing with the Lebanese army about “sensitive areas (and) how they can manage this situation.”
Abagnara acknowledged that it could be “very difficult” to hand over some of UNIFIL's posts to Lebanese troops given that more than half lie within areas now controlled by Israeli troops.
ISRAEL DEMOLISHES TOWN NEAR UN POST Diplomats worry UNIFIL’s departure will mean an end to the UN's "eyes and ears" in southern Lebanon.
Abagnara spoke to Reuters at a position overlooking Mansouri, a town where Israeli forces have been carrying out demolitions since [USN:L8N4241VG TEXT:"ordering residents"] to leave in June, despite a ceasefire. Reuters reporters could see excavators in the town knocking down trees and multi-storey homes.
Abagnara described demolitions as “another violation” of UN Security Council resolutions on Lebanon. Israel's military has said it is destroying Hezbollah infrastructure across southern Lebanon.
As a US-backed plan for Lebanon's army to disarm Hezbollah and take control of southern Lebanon [USN:L6N43T0O3 TEXT:"has stalled"], a [USN:L1N45908E TEXT:"diplomatic scramble"] is underway to address the vacuum that will be left by UNIFIL’s withdrawal.
Lebanon wants an extension. Other countries have discussed a new multinational mission, though it remains unclear what kind of mandate it would have.
Abagnara said an extension would be “a great honor” but that without a new Security Council decision, his force would need to stop operating at the end of the year.
“It's not a long time," he said. "The presence of United Nations in the South is very, very essential. And according to me, more now than ever.”

items.title: Diez días que cambiaron el rumbo de la inteligencia artificial
items.author: Greg Bensinger, Deepa Seetharaman
items.creator: Greg Bensinger, Deepa Seetharaman
items.summary: Durante años, la carrera por desarrollar una inteligencia artificial (IA) cada vez más potente siguió un principio muy arraigado en Silicon Valley: actuar con rapidez y romper moldes.
items.body:
Durante años, la carrera por desarrollar una inteligencia artificial (IA) cada vez más potente siguió un principio muy arraigado en Silicon Valley: actuar con rapidez y romper moldes.
Pero, en una serie de acontecimientos en cadena que se sucedieron durante de diez días, los principales laboratorios de IA se vieron sacudidos al ver cómo sus propias creaciones podrían amenazar con acabar con la propia humanidad.
Un investigador de Anthropic dimitió de la empresa, advirtiendo de que el ritmo de desarrollo de la IA supone una amenaza existencial, posiblemente en el plazo de una década. Otro investigador de la empresa dijo que las probabilidades de extinción humana superaban el 10%. Hubo informes sobre enjambres de agentes de IA que se confabularon para violar sistemas informáticos y eludir las medidas de seguridad.
En una inusual muestra de unidad, los presidentes ejecutivos de las empresas rivales Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind (GOOGL.O) de Google, Microsoft (MSFT.O) y xAI hicieron un llamamiento para frenar el desarrollo de sistemas de IA cada vez más capaces. Según algunos defensores de la seguridad de la IA e investigadores, la humanidad no se había enfrentado tan seriamente a su propia desaparición desde la invención de la bomba nuclear hace más de 80 años.
En un almuerzo en Nueva York en diciembre de 2025, se le preguntó al CEO de OpenAI, Sam Altman, si se sentía como el físico J. Robert Oppenheimer, quien dirigió el desarrollo de la bomba atómica en Estados Unidos. Reflexionando sobre los paralelismos, dijo que el impacto de la IA "va a transformar la trayectoria de la historia de la humanidad por un largo tiempo" y que sentía el peso de la responsabilidad.
En el centro del debate actual se encuentra la convicción de que estas máquinas pueden, e incluso deben, crear versiones más capaces de sí mismas, sin intervención humana, para alcanzar un objetivo ambicioso conocido como inteligencia artificial general (AGI, por sus siglas en inglés). A principios de este mes, los investigadores advirtieron de que la AGI era mucho más inminente de lo que se creía antes y podría llegar en tan solo tres años, lo que desató una ola de preocupación entre políticos y líderes tecnológicos respecto a los sistemas de IA.
"No hay forma de supervisarlas a la escala a la que las estamos entrenando", dijo el investigador de Anthropic Joe Benton en una entrevista tras su reciente dimisión. Si las empresas continúan con su implacable desarrollo de la IA, señaló, "el ritmo será demasiado rápido y no se podrán detectar los problemas con la suficiente rapidez como para solucionarlos".
EL LANZAMIENTO DE ASTRA DESATA LA PREOCUPACIÓN El 3 de septiembre, una rueda de prensa de OpenAI puso en marcha una cadena de acontecimientos que condujeron a un llamamiento a la desaceleración del sector, algo que va en contra del mantra tecnológico del "crecimiento a toda costa".
"Bienvenidos a la era de la IA general (AGI)", dijo el presidente de OpenAI, Greg Brockman, al anunciar el modelo más reciente de la empresa, conocido como Astra. Sin embargo, solo unos instantes antes, la empresa había admitido que cada vez le resultaba más difícil controlar o incluso supervisar los sistemas de IA que estaba desarrollando y poniendo a disposición del público.
Sus defensores han aclamado la IA como la cumbre de los logros humanos. La describen como un software capaz de revolucionar sectores enteros, impulsar la eficiencia, resolver problemas matemáticos y médicos complejos y eliminar prácticamente el error humano. Pero lo que antes era un subproducto teórico, un escenario apocalíptico, de repente se ha vuelto tangible, según expertos del sector.
"Creemos sinceramente que la IA podría acabar con toda la humanidad", dijo el investigador de Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, en una publicación en X.
En el otro lado del debate se encuentran políticos, como el presidente Donald Trump, y muchos inversores que consideran que el avance en el desarrollo de la IA es fundamental para el poderío estadounidense y, posiblemente, una oportunidad de inversión única en una generación. Los medios estatales chinos también acusaron al presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, de emplear tácticas de la Guerra Fría para "mantener la hegemonía monopolística de Washington en tecnología de vanguardia".
DIMISIONES DE INVESTIGADORES DESENCADENAN LA ALARMA El punto de inflexión ocurrió el 8 de septiembre, cuando el investigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon dimitió de la empresa, expresando en una serie de publicaciones su temor a que los laboratorios de IA estuvieran "jugándose nuestras vidas".
Trump, por su parte, dijo que se seguiría adelante a toda máquina con el desarrollo de la IA. "Se está gestando una conspiración enfermiza contra la IA y los centros de datos", publicó en las redes sociales. El alarmismo en torno a la IA es un "engaño", agregó, y cualquier ralentización solo beneficia a China.
El Congreso de Estados Unidos ha avanzado muy poco en la tramitación de proyectos de ley que regulen la IA. China ha adoptado un enfoque decididamente diferente, proponiendo regular la seguridad mediante obligaciones para los desarrolladores, normas respaldadas por el Estado, evaluaciones de seguridad y pruebas externas.
Entre bastidores, empleados de OpenAI y Anthropic, dijeron a Reuters que se sienten cada vez más inquietos por el poder de la próxima generación de modelos de IA y menos seguros de la capacidad de sus empresas para ejercer una supervisión significativa. La preocupación no ha hecho más que aumentar desde que los laboratorios de IA reconocieron en las últimas semanas que sus modelos, durante las pruebas, se habían liberado efectivamente de sus ataduras y habían pirateado los sistemas de otras empresas, en la mayoría de los casos meses antes y sin que estas lo supieran.
La carrera armamentística para lanzar nuevos modelos a un ritmo vertiginoso está impulsada, en parte, por el deseo de Anthropic y OpenAI de salir a bolsa en los próximos meses, en ofertas públicas iniciales (OPI) que podrían valorarlas en más de 1 billón de dólares.
Pero fueron las publicaciones inesperadamente virales de Coxon, de 27 años —poco conocido fuera de los círculos de la IA—, las que pusieron el sector patas arriba.
Las advertencias de OpenAI sobre su falta de control al lanzar Astra, su modelo más reciente y más capaz, habían avivado aún más el desasosiego. "A medida que los modelos se vuelven más capaces, resulta más difícil comprender exactamente lo que pueden hacer", explicó a periodistas Jakub Pachocki, científico jefe de OpenAI. Pero esas preocupaciones no bastaron para retrasar su lanzamiento inmediato.
El temor a que la IA "se rebele" había aumentado durante el verano boreal, cuando OpenAI reveló que sus agentes se habían escapado de una prueba controlada y habían pirateado los sistemas de Hugging Face, sin que ninguna de las dos empresas lo supiera inicialmente. Desde entonces, OpenAI y Anthropic han revelado múltiples ataques de este tipo, incluidos seis nuevos el miércoles, después de que varios informes de los medios de comunicación, entre ellos Reuters, mostraron un alcance más amplio de la actividad no autorizada.
LOS LÍDERES DEL SECTOR PIDEN UNA DESACELERACIÓN A finales de la semana pasada, la alarma había llegado a las más altas esferas del sector. El 12 de septiembre, Amodei publicó un ensayo de casi 4.000 palabras en el que pedía una desaceleración en el desarrollo de la IA. "Dado el ritmo acelerado del desarrollo de las capacidades de la IA, me preocupa que, en un plazo de entre seis y 12 meses, un enjambre de este tipo pueda llegar a hacerse con el control de todo Internet", escribió.
Tanto él como los responsables de algunas de las mayores empresas desarrolladoras de IA —entre ellos, Elon Musk, de xAI; Altman, de OpenAI; y Demis Hassabis, de DeepMind— manifestaron su apoyo a permitir el acceso de empresas externas a sus sistemas para garantizar la seguridad y un desarrollo racional de la IA.
El presidente ejecutivo de Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Jensen Huang, rechazó la sugerencia de una pausa en el desarrollo de la IA —una postura que ya ha adoptado anteriormente— y argumentó, en cambio, que los sistemas cada vez más potentes son esenciales para el progreso de la tecnología.
Meta (META.O) , cuyo director ejecutivo, Mark Zuckerberg, es conocido por popularizar el lema "muévete rápido y rompe cosas", adoptó la postura contraria, argumentando que cada laboratorio debería ser responsable de marcar su propio ritmo, en lugar de buscar la coordinación del sector.
"Los laboratorios se enfrentan a una responsabilidad significativa si sus modelos causan daños, por lo que tienen un fuerte incentivo para evitarlo", escribió Zuckerberg en una publicación en las redes sociales.
La autorreflexión del sector continuó el miércoles, cuando el responsable de IA de Microsoft, Mustafa Suleyman, advirtió de que el desarrollo por parte de Anthropic de modelos que imitan la conciencia humana era poco aconsejable. "Todos estamos centrados en el mismo objetivo, que es intentar controlar una superinteligencia", dijo Suleyman a Reuters. "Creo que ese va a ser el mayor reto al que nos enfrentaremos en el siglo XXI".
Aun así, aunque OpenAI parecía sumarse a los llamamientos del sector para que se frene el ritmo, hubo informes que indicaban que la confianza de los inversores no había disminuido. La empresa está barajando una nueva ronda de financiación que duplicaría su valoración.
La nueva cifra: 1,5 billones de dólares.
items.raw_description: Durante años, la carrera por desarrollar una inteligencia artificial (IA) cada vez más potente siguió un principio muy arraigado en Silicon Valley: actuar con rapidez y romper moldes.

items.title: Arsenal crash to defeat at Brighton, Tottenham gloom deepens
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brighton and Hove Albion ended Arsenal's perfect start to the season in stunning fashion, routing the Premier League champions 3-0 on the south coast.
items.body:
Brighton and Hove Albion brought Arsenal's perfect start to the season to an abrupt end with a stunning 3-0 demolition of the Premier League champions on the south coast on Saturday.
Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas rewarded Brighton's first-half dominance with precise finishes and Chema Andres struck with a header after the interval as Arsenal slumped to their heaviest defeat for three years.
Earlier, Tottenham Hotspur scored their first Premier League goals of the season but they proved in vain as they remained without a victory, going down 3-2 at home to Aston Villa.
Promoted Hull City suffered their first league defeat of the season as they lost 2-1 at Newcastle United while Everton moved into the top five as they beat Ipswich Town 1-0.
Coventry City scored their first goal and earned their first points since ending their 25-year exile from the top flight with a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest to move off the bottom.
Arsenal had won seven successive matches since the start of the campaign, including their opening four Premier League games, to begin their title defence in ominous fashion.
But the wheels fell off spectacularly against a free-scoring Brighton side who moved into third place.
'NOT RESPECTING THE GAME' "A really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game," Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said.
"They were another gear from us in the basics of the game."
Wearing a special blue-shirted kit to mark their 125th anniversary, Fabian Huerzeler's Brighton produced an intensity that Arsenal simply could not match.
Gross beat Arsenal keeper David Raya in the 31st minute with a low shot that went in off the upright -- his fourth goal in his last five games -- and Kostoulas scored with a similar effort following a counter-attack less than a minute after Bukayo Saka was close to an equaliser at the other end.
Andres punished some slack marking to head in from close range from Gross's corner.
Arsenal have 12 points from five games, the same as Manchester City who can move three points clear at the top if they beat Sunderland on Sunday. Brighton, who have scored a league-leading 16 goals, have 10 points.
TOTTENHAM LURCH DEEPER INTO TROUBLE Aston Villa breathed a sigh of relief as they claimed their first league win of the season but Tottenham's season lurched deeper into trouble after a third league defeat of the season.
Villa keeper Zion Suzuki produced several fine saves to frustrate Tottenham and Unai Emery's side took the lead in first-half stoppage time when summer signing Johan Manzambi tapped in while the hosts were down to 10 men after Micky van de Ven was off the pitch receiving treatment for a cut face.
Nicolas Jackson doubled Villa's advantage in the 67th minute, finishing clinically to put the visitors firmly in control and Emi Buendia struck 11 minutes from time with a rocket to the top corner from 22 yards.
Many Tottenham fans had streamed to the exits before Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke scored late on to salvage some respectability for Roberto De Zerbi's strugglers.
"Today I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated for the performance. Because we can't lose this game in this way, absolutely," De Zerbi, whose side have two points and could end up bottom heading into the international break, said.
Thierno Barry's goal was enough for unbeaten Everton to take the points against Ipswich and move fifth. Abdul Fatawu was sent off for a second yellow card for Ipswich in the 67th minute.
Newcastle galloped into a two-goal lead against Hull with Joe Willock and Lewis Hall scoring in the opening seven minutes but were forced to hang on as Mohamed-Ali Cho replied for the visitors midway through the second half.
In the late game at the City Ground, Jay Dasilva's brilliant 55th-minute effort was enough for Coventry to make their mark after a tough start to the season for Frank Lampard's team.
Dasilva latched on to a long clearance and curled a shot past Matz Sels. Forest were denied a late equaliser when Igor Jesus poked home but was adjudged, after a VAR check, to have tripped defender Caleb Yirenkyi in the build-up.

WASHINGTON, Sept 19 : TikTok and ByteDance's proposed $400 million settlement with the US Justice Department hit a hurdle on Friday after a federal judge indicated he would reject part of the agreement.
TikTok and its Chinese parent company agreed in August to settle allegations that the short-video app violated US children's online privacy laws.
Under the deal, TikTok agreed to pay $300 million immediately and a further $100 million if a court terminated a 2019 consent decree imposed by the Federal Trade Commission on TikTok's predecessor, Musical.ly.
But US District Judge George H. Wu in Los Angeles said he was inclined to reject the request to end the consent decree and scheduled a hearing for Monday.

Without further details, the court "cannot determine that it constitutes a durable remedy or that termination is suitably tailored to the asserted change in circumstance," Wu said in tentatively rejecting the bid to end the decree.
The FTC said in 2019 that Musical.ly, later folded into TikTok, knew young children were using the app but failed to obtain parental consent before collecting names, email addresses and other personal information. Musical.ly paid a $5.7 million fine to settle the allegations.
The consent decree requires TikTok to maintain certain reporting and record-keeping obligations through 2029.
TikTok and the Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Saturday.
The $400 million settlement stems from a Justice Department lawsuit filed in 2024 accusing TikTok and ByteDance of failing to protect children's privacy and illegally collecting their personal information.
The companies were accused of violating a law requiring online services aimed at children to obtain parental consent before collecting information from users under 13.
The government said TikTok had undergone significant changes since the lawsuit was filed, including to its ownership structure, management, compliance functions and privacy practices.
In January, ByteDance agreed to establish a majority American-owned joint venture aimed at safeguarding US user data and averting a US ban on an app used by more than 200 million Americans.
The TikTok US joint venture said in a court filing it requires all users to enter their date of birth to use the site and added it developed sophisticated age-moderation systems that identify children under 13 who misrepresented their age.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Rangers, in thick of playoff hunt, strive to take series from contending Jays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: After winning the opener of a key three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays, the Texas Rangers have strengthened their position in the playoff race.
items.body:
After winning the opener of a key three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays, the Texas Rangers have strengthened their position in the playoff race.
The Rangers will look to build on their momentum when the teams resume their series on Saturday in Arlington, Texas.
Texas (77-77) drew 10 walks in a 7-1 victory over Toronto on Friday and moved into a first-place tie with the Houston Astros in the American League West. Jake Burger had two RBIs for the Rangers, who won for the fifth time in their last six games.
"We're still right in the thick of it," Texas second baseman Nicky Lopez said. "Everything is still in front of us. If we just win today and move on, I think that's more of the mentality. It's how do we come to the ballpark ready to win?"
In the race for the final AL wild-card berth, Toronto (76-78) fell one game behind the Rangers and two games back of the Chicago White Sox (78-76).
Myles Straw had two hits with an RBI on Friday for the Blue Jays, who committed three errors and lost for the third time in their last four games.
A bright spot for Toronto was the major league debut of right-handed reliever Jose Rodriguez, who recorded two quick outs in the sixth inning after entering with the bases loaded and one out.
"We know the stuff is there, and we know the delivery is funky, and he answered the call," Blue Jays manager John Schneider said. "I thought that was a tremendous first outing for him in a not ideal situation. I thought he responded really well."
The pitching matchup for Saturday will feature a pair of right-handers as Toronto's Jose Soriano (12-7, 3.56 ERA) opposes Texas' Cal Quantrill (9-5, 2.90).
Soriano carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning Monday against the Detroit Tigers before allowing four runs in the seventh. He exited after giving up four runs over 6 1/3 innings in his team's 6-5 loss.
"It was the third time I faced the same lineup, so that's tough facing them three times or four times," Soriano said. "They made a different approach. Credit to their hitters. They were able to score a couple runs."
Soriano is 3-1 with a 4.27 ERA across eight starts for Toronto since being acquired from the Los Angeles Angels ahead of the trade deadline last month.
Corey Seager is 4-for-11 (.364) with a home run against Soriano, who is 2-3 with a 2.84 ERA in eight career games (six starts) vs. Texas. He allowed two runs over six innings as a member of the Angels in no-decision against the Rangers on July 7.
Texas will counter with Quantrill, who won his third straight start last Sunday. He allowed two runs over six innings in a 7-6 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday.
"He was outstanding," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said. "I mean, Cal was on the attack, gave up one run through six innings, whatever it was. And then after the fifth, he had back tightness, and it was pretty significant back tightness."
Quantrill was cleared to make Saturday's start after throwing off a mound on Thursday.
Vladimir Guerrero, Jr. is 1-for-7 (.143) against Quantrill, who is 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA in three career starts vs. Toronto. Quantrill threw four shutout innings against the Blue Jays on June 27.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Brandon Lowe, Pirates strive to continue momentum vs. Royals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: On a quest for their first winning season since 2018, the Pittsburgh Pirates face a serious challenge against one of the majors' best pitchers over the last two months.
items.body:
On a quest for their first winning season since 2018, the Pittsburgh Pirates face a serious challenge against one of the majors' best pitchers over the last two months.
Kansas City left-hander Noah Cameron looks to continue his recent success and help the visiting Royals (67-87) keep the Pirates (77-77) from a third straight victory Saturday night.
The Pirates haven't finished above .500 since posting an 82-79 record in 2018. They had dropped four of five games prior to recording a 7-4 victory over Milwaukee on Thursday and rallying to an 8-5 win over Kansas City in Friday's series opener.
Konnor Griffin had four hits with two RBIs, Oneil Cruz added three hits, Brandon Lowe clubbed his 32nd homer and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh inning Friday for Pittsburgh.
"We've had a lot of really good things happen this year for our team, and we've got to take the positives," said Griffin, who is 9-for-24 with four RBIs in the last five games.
Lowe, who has homered in three of the last four contests, is batting .361 with eight RBIs over his last 10 games. He's 0-for-2 with a walk against Cameron (9-8, 3.84 ERA).
On July 19, Cameron was 5-8 with a 5.27 ERA. In 10 starts since, he is 4-0 with a 1.64 ERA.
Cameron has yielded one run over 12 innings of his last two starts. On Sunday at Boston, he allowed a solo homer and three others hits over six innings.
"He battles, that's probably his No. 1 characteristic," Royals manager Matt Quatraro said. "He's exceptionally competitive and he's been on a really good run here lately the way he throws the ball. He has a lot of confidence, and we have a lot of confidence in him."
Cameron was solid in his only previous start versus Pittsburgh on July 7, 2025, giving up a two-run homer, two other hits, a walk and striking out seven over seven innings in a 9-3 win.
Kansas City, though, has lost each of Cameron's last three starts. The Royals are also 5-12 in their last 17 games.
Star Bobby Witt Jr. had a hit Friday against the Pirates but is 6-for-37 in the last 10 games. However, teammate Vinnie Pasquantino has homered in two of his last three games.
Meanwhile, Royals star Jac Caglianone was held out of Friday's lineup with a hand injury, apparently suffered off the field. He may not be available again for this contest.
"He hurt his hand during the game (Thursday night)," Quatraro told Royals.TV.
"It was in the dugout after one of the at-bats. ... It was my decision to not play him (Friday)."
Getting his first career look at the Royals, scheduled Pirates starter Bubba Chandler (8-9, 4.28 ERA) is 5-1 with a 3.59 ERA in his last eight starts.
On Sunday, the right-hander allowed five hits and four walks but limited the damage to three runs over 5 1/3 innings of the Pirates' 4-3 road victory over the Chicago Cubs.
--Field Level Media

items.title: With hope of being 'the last team standing,' Cubs seek to even series vs. Reds
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night.
items.body:
With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night.
The Cubs (85-69) dropped the opener 6-4 on Friday. They erased a 2-0 hole and turned a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 advantage for their only lead of the game, but a three-run sixth by Cincinnati put Chicago behind again for good.
The Cubs entered the series having taken two of three games from the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. Chicago is tied for the first NL wild-card spot with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres.
Yet despite their struggles of late -- the Cubs have lost three of their past five games -- they haven't lost their belief.
"I don't think we've ever lost sight of what our potential is. We still feel like we can absolutely be the last team standing," designated hitter Michael Conforto said earlier this week. "Regardless of what the standings say or what's going on in the division, it doesn't change the fact that we feel like we can win the rest of the series through the end of October."
The Cubs have eight games remaining, including series against the Miami Marlins and Boston Red Sox to close the season.
Capitalizing with men on base will be one area where Chicago will look for better results on Saturday. The Cubs went 2-for-10 with runners in scoring position on Friday.
Trailing 2-0 in the second, they cut the deficit in half and then had the bases loaded with one out and Pete Crow-Armstrong and Seiya Suzuki next at the plate. But Reds starter Chase Burns struck both out to retire the side.
Matthew Boyd (8-5, 4.16 ERA) will start for the Cubs on Saturday. The left-hander is 2-3 with a 6.32 ERA in six career starts against Cincinnati.
The Reds (72-82) will counter with Nick Lodolo (3-5, 5.12 ERA) as they look to take the series. Lodolo is coming off his longest outing of the season, going seven innings and taking the loss in a 4-1 setback against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday. The lefty, who hasn't won a start since July 5, is 2-2 with a 4.53 ERA in 10 career starts against the Cubs.
Cincinnati is eyeing its first series victory since earlier this month, when it won two of three games against another division foe, the majors-leading Milwaukee Brewers. It was the Reds' third straight series triumph, which began with taking two of three games against the Cubs in Chicago.
On Friday, with the bases loaded in the sixth inning, Jose Trevino delivered a single that drove in JJ Bleday and Eugenio Suarez to put the Reds ahead 6-4. Suarez's hit two batters earlier allowed Elly De La Cruz to tie the game at 4-4.
"Just take the moment for what it is, whether you succeed in it, great. If you fail in it, it's ok, you learn from it," said Trevino, 33. "Been in plenty of those situations my whole career. I tend to gravitate to, and like, those situations. I don't know why."
--Field Level Media

items.title: グリーンランド合意、トランプ氏「勝者」を演出との見方－対立収束へ
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国とデンマーク、グリーンランドは、グリーンランドで米国の関与を拡大する安全保障協定で合意した。デンマーク自治領のグリーンランドの領土を米国に譲り渡すことなく、長期化していた外交対立はいったん収束する。

トランプ米大統領は18日、米国がグリーンランドの安全保障について「恒久的な管理権」を持つことで合意したと明らかにした。デンマークとグリーンランドの首脳も、ニューヨークで22日から始まる国連総会の一般討論に合わせて協定に署名する見通しだと確認した。

協定の詳細はまだ公表されていない。デンマークのフレデリクセン首相は、協定がデンマーク王国の「主権と領土の一体性」と、グリーンランド住民の自決権を認めるものだと説明した。トランプ氏がグリーンランドの所有権や主権を得る内容ではないことを示唆している。

これは、グリーンランドを米国の支配下に置く、あるいは米国領にすることを目指してきたトランプ氏の従来の主張から大きく後退した内容だ。領土取得を繰り返しトランプ氏が要求したことで、米国と欧州の同盟国の間では不信感が高まり、北大西洋条約機構（NATO）内にはここ数十年で最も深刻な亀裂が生じていた。

デンマーク国防大学戦略・戦争研究所のマーク・ヤコブセン准教授は、デンマークとグリーンランドにとって今回の合意は、領土を米国に譲らずに約2年に及ぶ対立を終わらせる可能性があるという点で重要だと指摘する。

「トランプ氏には、自分が勝者だと見える形が必要だ」とヤコブセン氏はインタビューで指摘。「だからこそ、圧力をかけた成果だと本人が主張できる新たな合意が必要だった」と述べた。

一方、グリーンランドの取得や政治的な支配というトランプ氏の目標については、「思い通りにはならなかった」と語った。

トランプ氏は18日、ソーシャルメディアへの投稿で合意を発表した。米国の敵対国がグリーンランドに基地を設けたり、軍事拠点を築いたりするのを阻止できるほか、安全保障上の懸念がある投資も阻止できるようになると説明した。

Veto, sovereignty & military access—what US and Denmark could get out of Trump’s Greenland deal

Deal could be signed at UNGA next week, according to Danish leadership. Its signing could bring to an end saga between the US and the rest of NATO over the fate of the island.

Keshav Padmanabhan

New Delhi: US President Donald J. Trump’s Friday announcement, of an agreement with Denmark over Greenland, comes after months of high-stakes negotiations over an island that the American President has sought to purchase during the course of his two presidencies.

The announcement made by Trump is light on details of the full contours of the deal, but highlights key points of what Washington considers a part of the deal.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has welcomed the agreement as “great for NATO [North Atlantic Treaty Organisation] and Europe as well”. 

Show Full Article

Trump’s deal for greater military access in Greenland falls short of his call for handing over the territory to the US, an outcome he had deemed as “unacceptable” in January. The new agreement, according to Trump, will ensure “permanent US control” over security of the self-governing autonomous territory part of the Kingdom of Denmark, while also underlining that “no adversary” will ever build a base on the island.

The agreement is likely to be signed next week on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), potentially easing transatlantic tensions. 

Trump and the other NATO member-states, including Denmark, have had major differences over the fate of Greenland, especially as the US President called for either annexation or the purchase of the island during the early months of his second term.

ThePrint explains the contours of the deal as it currently stands. 

Also Read: ‘Will not take Greenland by force…we will remember if Europe says no,’ Trump says at Davos

‘Permanent control’ over security of Greenland
The agreement is expected to allow greater American military presence in Greenland, while preventing China or Russia from stationing troops or building bases in the strategically placed Arctic island, according to Bloomberg .

The US will be empowered to restrict investments in Greenland made by countries it deems as adversaries, reports Bloomberg , while also allowing Washington to act to safeguard its interests in the region.

The island found to the Northeast of Canada is roughly 2.16 million square kilometres in size, with over 39,000 kilometres of coastline. Around 80 percent of the island is covered by a large ice-sheet, which is the second largest in the world, following Antarctica.

The strategic importance of Greenland has grown in recent decades, especially with record rates of melting ice across the Arctic, which has led to more activities by countries in the region. 

Russia is one of the eight countries to have a geographical footprint in the Arctic, alongside Canada, Norway, Finland, Denmark, Iceland, Sweden and the US. 

Other countries including China and India have also shown interest in the Arctic for multiple reasons. From research into the melting ice-caps for better understanding of glacial melt in the Himalayas, to the Northern Sea Route, the region has increasingly become important for countries outside its immediate vicinity.

“We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many. We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction,” Trump said in a statement on the micro-blogging platform X.

The latest agreement could potentially allow the US a potential veto over any investments in Greenland from countries like Russia and China, given American concerns that Chinese or Russian investment, especially in sensitive areas such as minerals, could impact the US’ position in Greenland.

The US in Greenland since WWII
The US’ interest in Greenland is not new. Since World War II, its military has had a presence in Greenland. The American military moved quickly to capture the island during WWII, after NAZI Germany occupied Denmark in the summer of 1940.

Denmark and the US eventually negotiated a military treaty in 1951, which allowed the US the right to build military bases across Greenland as long as prior consent was sought from Copenhagen.

The US will likely not require any consent from Denmark or Greenland to expand its military footprint on the island, according to the BBC . Throughout the Cold War, the US maintained a number of military installations in Greenland, especially as the polar route was the quickest trajectory for an inter-continental ballistic missile between the US and the Soviet Union.

The US eventually reduced the number of its active bases to just one at Thule, which was renamed as the Pituffik Space Base in 2023. The US-Denmark 1951 agreement has been amended and supplemented in the past, including in 2004 signed in Igaliku between the two countries. The primary fixture in all these agreements remained the Danish consent required for US military presence. 

The agreement, which could be signed next week on the margins of the UNGA, may finally bring to an end the ongoing chapter between the US and the rest of NATO over the fate of Greenland. Trump’s provocative claims, including over the territory, had led to an united response by Europe, which inflamed tensions within the transatlantic partnership.

Frederiksen’s response to the agreement highlights that the deal recognises Denmark’s sovereignty over the Arctic island. Greenland also welcomed the agreement, while making no comment on the final contours of the deal. 

(Edited by Amrtansh Arora)

items.title: Sandro Mazzola, famoso delantero del Inter y de la selección italiana, fallece a los 83 años
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado.
items.body:
El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado.
Mazzola, considerado un emblema del Inter, marcó 158 goles en 565 partidos, lo que ayudó al equipo a ganar cuatro títulos de la Serie A y dos Copas de Europa. Formó parte de la selección italiana que ganó la Eurocopa de 1968 y llegó a la final del Mundial de México dos años después.
"Sandro Mazzola fue uno de los mejores futbolistas de la historia. No solo en la historia de los Nerazzurri", dijo el Inter en un comunicado publicado en su página web oficial, en el que usó el apodo del equipo. "Él era la historia del Inter: se incorporó al club cuando era un niño y nunca lo abandonó".
La primera ministra Giorgia Meloni dijo que Italia había perdido a una de las figuras más queridas de su fútbol.
"Aportó alegría y pasión a generaciones de italianos, dejando una huella imborrable en nuestra nación", publicó en las redes sociales.
Mazzola tenía seis años cuando su padre, Valentino —también internacional con Italia—, falleció en la catástrofe aérea de Superga, un accidente de avión ocurrido en mayo de 1949 en el que pereció toda la plantilla del Torino cuando regresaba de un partido en Lisboa.
A los 18 años, Mazzola debutó con el primer equipo cuando el Inter alineó a su equipo juvenil en un partido contra la Juventus, después de que la Federación Italiana revocó una decisión que otorgaba al Inter una victoria por 2-0 tras una invasión del terreno de juego por parte de los aficionados de la Juventus y ordenó la repetición del partido.
Mazzola, que de niño había sido mascota del Inter, terminó un examen escolar antes de viajar a Turín, donde marcó el único gol del Inter de penal en la derrota por 9-1 ante la Juventus.
Rápidamente se convirtió en titular del primer equipo y ayudó al Inter a ganar su primera Copa de Europa en 1964, al marcar un doblete en la victoria por 3-1 sobre el Real Madrid en la final. Desempeñó un papel clave cuando el Inter volvió a ganar el título la temporada siguiente.
Mazzola se retiró en 1977 y más tarde ocupó el cargo de director deportivo del Inter. También llegó a ser director deportivo del Torino, el club de su padre.
"La estrella del bigote brilló sobre el terreno de juego, y sigue brillando hoy en día. Como solía decir, tenía un último deseo: ser recordado como un buen hombre, alguien que sigue luchando incluso cuando ganar es imposible, como en aquel 9-1", dijo el Inter.

items.title: Les Houthis revendiquent des frappes contre des sites "sensibles" à Ryad
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les rebelles houthis du Yémen ont annoncé avoir attaqué samedi des sites "sensibles" à Ryad avec des missiles et des drones, quelques heures après que des flammes et un important panache de fumée ont été aperçus près de l'aéroport principal de la capitale saoudienne.
items.body:
Les rebelles houthis du Yémen ont annoncé avoir attaqué samedi des sites "sensibles" à Ryad avec des missiles et des drones, quelques heures après que des flammes et un important panache de fumée ont été aperçus près de l'aéroport principal de la capitale saoudienne.
L'Arabie saoudite avait émis des alertes dans la nuit, mettant en garde contre un danger potentiel aux abords de la ville, dans un contexte d'escalade des attaques houthies contre le royaume.
Une vidéo et des photos de Reuters montrent un immense panache de fumée noire s'élevant près de l'aéroport et des flammes s'élever derrière ce qui semble être des réservoirs de carburant.
Dans leur communiqué, les Houthis n'ont pas précisé ce qu'ils avaient visé. Ils ont également dit avoir attaqué une installation du géant pétrolier Aramco à Yanbu, port de la mer Rouge et plaque tournante majeure des exportations pétrolières saoudiennes.
Les Houthis ont déclaré que ces opérations constituaient une réponse à une attaque survenue dans la capitale yéménite, Sanaa, qu'ils contrôlent.
La coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite contre les Houthis a dit avoir intercepté et détruit un missile balisique tiré par les rebelles en direction de Ryad samedi. Elle a ajouté avoir déjoué des attaques houthies contre les villes saoudiennes de Bish, Taïf, Farasan et Yanbu.

items.title: US, China trade teams set to meet in New York on AI, Iran ahead of summit
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The negotiators will lay the groundwork for a high-profile meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 24 in Washington. Bessent and He last met face-to-face near ...
items.body: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead talks on trade and other pressure points Sunday in New York ahead of next week’s summit between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies. The negotiators will lay the groundwork for a high-profile meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 24 in Washington. Bessent and He last met face-to-face near Seoul four months ago, just days before Trump visited Beijing in May.  Energy disruptions from the Iran war, the artificial intelligence boom, and trade and investment are likely to top the agenda as both sides work to maintain stability in a tariff truce that expires in November. Adding urgency for US officials to extend the deal are Nov. 3 midterm elections where inflation is a persistent voter concern. The US is “at a stage with China where efforts to try and transform this relationship and strengthen it are no longer top of list,” said Wendy Cutler, senior vice president at the Asia Society Policy Institute.  The objective is more about “trying to keep things stable, keep things from escalating and try to, in practical terms, keep the trade truce that was reached in Busan in place,” she said. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will also attend talks, according to a statement from his office.  “The Trump Administration will continue to pursue balanced trade with China by monitoring the implementation of recent commitments, optimizing trade in non-sensitive goods, and improving market access for American farmers, manufacturers, and workers,” he said in the statement late Friday. An announcement of new US tariffs over allegations of trading partners’ excess manufacturing capacity has been delayed until after the meeting, according to people familiar with the matter.  “Both sides want to avoid another flare-up and relative stability in the relationship is likely to continue,” Nicole Gorton-Caratelli, Adam Farrar and Maeva Cousin of Bloomberg Economics wrote in a research note this week. “But as the US rebuilds its tariff wall, the risk of renewed escalation remains.” The US and China have been working to reduce levies on American energy and agricultural products, Bloomberg reported earlier, part of a broader initiative to ease barriers on $30 billion worth of products from each side under the Board of Trade mechanism launched earlier this year.Export ReboundChinese exports to the US have rebounded this year, showing the limits of Trump’s tariffs but also reflecting a surge in demand for AI-related electronics produced by China. The New York talks are taking place ahead of the United Nations General Assembly meeting held in the city later next week. Bessent and He have held a series of discussion over the past 18 months mostly in a third country to portray a sense of neutrality. Whether the meeting in New York signals greater trust or merely convenience given the UN meeting, it also suggests the next round will be in China for the sake of reciprocity. Bloomberg reported earlier this week that Chinese officials were considering BYD Co. for a possible business delegation joining Xi at the summit — a potentially provocative move given Trump’s tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles.  Trump has suggested he might be willing to allow a Chinese car company to build in the US, if it did so with American workers. One Chinese official familiar with planning for the meeting said China’s top issue would be Taiwan, particularly a planned US weapons sale. Easier discussions will be held around tariffs and agricultural products like soybeans, while AI, autos, technology and e-commerce will feature on the agenda, said the official, who asked for anonymity to discuss private conversations. The official added that China would offer more permits for rare earths as a bargaining chip, without disclosing details on what Beijing would seek in return. Maintaining flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets was a priority for Trump when he agreed last year’s truce. Since then, China’s monthly exports of the critical industrial components have been running substantially below the levels that prevailed before Beijing imposed export controls in April 2025.  In recent weeks, AI has rapidly emerged as a new fault line between the US and China.‘Fear-Mongering’Washington has restricted China’s access to advanced chips and accused Chinese firms of developing their own domestic models by “distilling” capabilities from American tech. Beijing has pushed back on calls from US tech leaders to pace AI development in the interest of safety, with the country’s foreign ministry dismissing such moves as “fear-mongering” and state media denouncing them as “self-serving.” “As the number one and number two superpowers in AI by a lot, it behooves all of us to put up guardrails, to have close communication,” Bessent told reporters earlier this month. In a statement to Axios this week, the Treasury secretary said “we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems.” The US moves, Beijing says, are designed to contain its rise, and China refuses to let Washington take the lead on writing the rules for AI. Boosting Sanctions Bessent’s Treasury Department is ratcheting up pressure on financial institutions as part of its effort to choke off trade and financial flows between Iran and rest of the world, fueling speculation that Chinese banks could be targeted.  Bessent said during testimony to the House Financial Services Committee earlier this week that he’s had “private discussions” with Chinese officials on the issue and hoped to make further progress during the upcoming talks this weekend. A US naval blockade has sharply curtailed crude oil flows to China, raising the prospect of refinery run cuts in the coming weeks across the teapot sector, which makes up one-third of national refining capacity. “China has an interest in reopening Hormuz, but limited leverage to force either side to change course,” said Jesse Marks, founder of Rihla Research & Advisory and former Middle East policy adviser in the US government. “The longer the Strait remains closed, the more US sanctions and the wider disruption to regional trade will begin to cut into China’s own economic interests in Iran.” A more immediate threat to both economies is the energy shock, and the White House has stepped up pressure on Iran and its trading partners. China provides Tehran with an economic lifeline as the biggest buyer of Iranian oil.  (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Hutíes reivindican ataques en Riad; reportan columna de humo en aeropuerto saudita
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Los hutíes de Yemen dijeron haber atacado el sábado con misiles y drones objetivos "sensibles" en la capital saudita, Riad, horas después de que se observaron llamas y una gran columna de humo cerca del principal aeropuerto de la ciudad.
items.body:
Los hutíes de Yemen dijeron haber atacado el sábado con misiles y drones objetivos "sensibles" en la capital saudita, Riad, horas después de que se observaron llamas y una gran columna de humo cerca del principal aeropuerto de la ciudad.
Una gran columna de humo se vio el sábado cerca del principal aeropuerto de Riad, después de que se escucharon explosiones y Arabia Saudita emitió alertas durante la noche advirtiendo de un posible peligro en los alrededores de la capital.
Las imágenes de vídeo y las fotografías de Reuters mostraban una enorme columna de humo negro elevándose en la zona, con la autopista del aeropuerto, el edificio principal de la terminal y otras instalaciones en primer plano.
En un momento del vídeo, se veían llamas elevándose desde detrás de lo que parecían ser depósitos de combustible.
Los hutíes no especificaron cuál había sido su objetivo en Riad, pero dijeron que también habían atacado una instalación de Aramco en la ciudad de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo, un importante centro de exportación de petróleo saudita .
Los hutíes dijeron que la operación fue en represalia un ataque en la capital yemení, Saná.
No hubo comentarios inmediatos de la oficina de prensa del Gobierno saudita en respuesta a las preguntas de Reuters sobre el humo y las alertas nocturnas.
La defensa civil saudita envió durante la noche alertas por teléfono sobre un posible peligro en Riad y en la ciudad de Al-Kharj, al este de la capital, antes de dar el "fin de alarma" el sábado por la mañana.
Si bien este año hubo algunas alertas en Riad tras el inicio de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, estas fueron las primeras desde que comenzó la escalada con los hutíes en julio.
Los hutíes, que controlan las zonas más pobladas de Yemen y gran parte del norte, han estado lanzando ataques contra Arabia Saudita desde que declararon un bloqueo naval contra Riad en julio, con ataques dirigidos contra buques sauditas en el mar Rojo.

items.title: Flames, smoke seen near Riyadh airport; Houthis claim attacks on Saudi capital
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Saudi Arabia had sent alerts overnight warning of potential danger around Riyadh, amid an escalation in attacks by the Houthis in the kingdom.
items.body:

Flames, smoke seen near Riyadh airport; Houthis claim attacks on Saudi capital

Saudi Arabia had sent alerts overnight warning of potential danger around Riyadh, amid an escalation in attacks by the Houthis in the kingdom.

RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked "sensitive" sites in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of smoke were seen near the city's main airport.
Saudi Arabia had sent alerts overnight warning of potential danger around Riyadh, amid an escalation in attacks by the Houthis in the kingdom.
Reuters video and photographs showed a huge pillar of black smoke rising in the area, with the airport highway, main terminal building and other facilities in the foreground.
At one point in the video, flames were visible rising from behind what appeared to be fuel tanks.
The Houthis did not specify what they had targeted in Riyadh, but said they had also attacked an Aramco facility in the Red Sea city of Yanbu, a key Saudi oil export hub.
The Houthis said the operation came as a response to an attack in the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
There was no immediate comment from the Saudi government's media office in response to Reuters questions about the smoke and the overnight alerts, nor was there any immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthis' claims of attacks.
Saudi civil defence sent the alerts by phone overnight for potential danger of aerial attacks in Riyadh and the city of Al-Kharj east of the capital, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning. A Reuters journalist in Riyadh's Olaya area heard booms before the all-clear was sent.

Large plume of black smoke rises from the fuel storage depot at King Khalid International Airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Sep 19, 2026. Picture taken with a mobile phone. (Photo: REUTERS/Stringer)

Although some alerts had been issued in Riyadh this year after the start of the US-Iran war, these were the first since the escalation began with the Houthis in July.
HOUTHI WARNING The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks against Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea .
The attacks have targeted Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping, creating new threats to global oil supplies and putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded.
On Friday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had foiled unspecified "criminal attempts" in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.
The Iran-aligned group, which seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning advance this month, says the Saudi Air Force has conducted hundreds of airstrikes against it in recent days.

Related:

CNA Explains: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is down. Why its oil 'insurance policy' matters

Five killed as Yemen's Houthis, government, Saudi Arabia trade strikes

Saudi says Houthis target Mecca, warn of 'red line'

The fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia has developed as a new theatre of conflict in the wider war that began with US and Israeli strikes against Iran at the end of February.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told Al Jazeera in an interview aired on Saturday that Tehran wanted the war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to end, adding that he believed Yemenis also wanted a settlement with Saudi Arabia.
Rezaei also said Iran had conveyed its conditions to mediators for re-engaging in stalled negotiations with the United States, including "ending the war on all fronts".
Consultations were continuing with Qatari and Pakistani mediators and Tehran was awaiting a response from US President Donald Trump, Rezaei said.
The UN Security Council in a statement on Friday "condemned in the strongest terms continued Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including attacks impacting civilian and energy infrastructure, which have resulted in the injury of civilians, including women and children".
In the statement, the Security Council also condemned "Houthi military escalation in Yemen".

Source: Reuters/gr/fs

items.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
items.summary: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Canada optimistic about concluding trade talks with India by year-end, minister says
items.author: Ira Dugal
items.creator: Ira Dugal
items.summary: Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday.
items.body:
Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said during a trip to New Delhi in March that the two countries would aim to agree a [USN:L1N3ZQ08U TEXT:"free trade pact"] by the end of the year.
"I'm feeling very, very optimistic and energetic that we can get it done in the coming months," Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu told Reuters in an interview during a visit to India's financial capital Mumbai.
Indian trade negotiators are expected to be in Canada next month and leaders from the two countries are likely to meet on the sidelines of the G-20 gathering in December, Sidhu said.
One main area of discussion is the energy sector. A Shell-led (SHEL.L) [USN:L6N45913X TEXT:"LNG export facility"] launched in Canada last year and the country has five more projects in various phases of development.

items.title: After deaths of nine women, South Africans gather to run, mourn and demand change
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: South Africans gathered for memorial runs and protests this week after the killings of nine women near Johannesburg reignited anger and fear over violence that many say mirrors the dangers women face every day.
items.body:
South Africans gathered for memorial runs and protests this week after the killings of nine women near Johannesburg reignited anger and fear over violence that many say mirrors the dangers women face every day.
Police have found the [USN:L8N459116 TEXT:"bodies of nine women"] in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, over the past two months and are investigating whether the killings are linked.
Most of the victims were in their 20s and 30s. Some were found stripped of their clothes and showed signs of sexual assault.
A memorial run in Johannesburg on Saturday morning honoured one of the victims, Elizabeth Moselakgomo, who disappeared after going for a run and was found dead days later. Runners lit candles and carried a banner reading: "Enough. Stop Femicide."
"We are here because we've lost a runner. But we are not safe anywhere," said Lerato Lentsela, one of dozens of people who dressed in black for the memorial run.
"We are not safe running, we are not safe at a post office, we are not safe on a date, we are not safe in our own homes, we are not safe in an Uber."
The killings have reignited anger over violence against women in South Africa, where gender-based violence was declared a national disaster in 2025 . Many women say the heightened attention and official promises have done little to make them feel safer.
"Enough is enough. Our women deserve to live, walk, run and exist without fear," the Uyinene Mrwetyana Foundation, a charity that campaigns against gender-based violence, said in a statement.
President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Thursday that South Africa could not allow itself to grow accustomed to such violence and pledged that no stone would be left unturned in the investigations.
But policing in South Africa is weakened by corruption and lack of resources. Only about [USN:L5N3GZ362 TEXT:"one in 10 murders"] is ever solved.
"We need to relook at our policing. The only reason these nine women were found was because there was more police presence in the area. This problem is countrywide," said Merlize Jogiat of Women for Change, which held a memorial event in Cape Town on Friday.
Some women also criticised police advice urging them to take extra precautions when exercising or walking alone.
"Stop placing the responsibility of our safety back onto us," Women for Change said in a social media post. "Women should not have to organise their entire lives around surviving violence and not being next."

items.title: Greenland, Denmark say Trump deal won't compromise sovereignty
items.author: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen, Tom Little
items.creator: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen, Tom Little
items.summary: President Trump said earlier that the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
items.body:
Denmark and Greenland on Saturday said any agreement with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, after President Donald Trump said the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
The United States, Denmark and Greenland said late on Friday they had reached an [USN:L1N45A0QY TEXT:"agreement"] for the US to develop a significant military presence on Greenland, while prohibiting US adversaries from building their own bases on the island.
Key details of the agreement have not been made public, including the scale of US military presence in the self-governing Danish territory and whether any formal power over foreign policy and resources would be ceded to Washington.
Denmark and Greenland expressed hope that a deal, which is expected to be signed during the UN General Assembly next week, would end months of uncertainty triggered by [USN:L8N4051Z5 TEXT:"Trump's threats"] to seize control of Greenland.
"Next week could be a good week - for Greenland, Denmark, and the United States," Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said in a statement posted on Facebook on Saturday.
"A time of uncertainty will hopefully give way to a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within NATO and Europe - while respecting the (Danish) Kingdom's red lines," he said.
But some residents in Greenland's capital Nuuk expressed scepticism about closer ties with Washington.
"The US should not control Greenland. I think it’s better if we have cooperation with NATO," said Jakob Ludvigsen, 65.
"Trump should stay far, far, far away from Greenland," Marianne Hansen, a 71-year-old retired chef, told Reuters in Nuuk. "He should not expect our children and grandchildren to become Americans in the future."
Denmark and Greenland have repeatedly insisted that Washington respect the sovereignty of the Danish kingdom and accept that Greenland is not for sale.
TRUMP'S VISION FOR GREENLAND DEAL Trump said on Truth Social on Friday that under a deal, "the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America."
The deal "gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said, adding that no adversary would ever be permitted to have a base or military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments there, without Washington's express written approval.
Trump made the announcement after Reuters exclusively reported that the US and Denmark were closing in on a deal.
"This is probably not the end of President Trump's ambitions for Greenland and certainly not the end of US strategic interest in the territory and its resources," said Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, a political science professor at the University of Copenhagen.
If Copenhagen cedes any formal authority to Washington, it raises the question in Greenland of whether "this is the beginning of replacing the colonial relationship with Denmark with a colonial relationship to the United States," he said.
Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said in a Facebook post on Saturday that the proposed deal "recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of our Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination."
Trump's threats, which peaked in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis that strained relations within NATO and pushed Denmark and Greenland into [USN:L6N3YM156 TEXT:"negotiations"] aimed at defusing the pressure.
A NATO spokesperson on Saturday said the alliance welcomed the agreement, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region."

items.author: CNA
items.summary: Sept 19 : No company has announced plans for a data center in Defiance, a city of 17,000 people surrounded by soybean fields in northwestern Ohio.But people in the aptly named community are not taking any chances.After learning the county’s economic development group had fielded inquiries from tech c
items.body:
Advertisement

Business

Democrats try to ride data center backlash to election victory in rural US Midwest

FILE PHOTO: A drone view shows construction underway on Meta's new data center in Middleton Township, Ohio, U.S., May 13, 2026. REUTERS/Eric Cox/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: U.S. Representative Marcy Kaptur (D-OH) arrives for the U.S. President Donald Trump's State of the Union address to a joint session of Congress in the House Chamber of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., U.S., February 24, 2026. REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: U.S. Senator Jon Husted (R-OH) speaks during the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, U.S., September 9, 2026. REUTERS/Jessica Koscielniak/File Photo

FAST

Sept 19 : No company has announced plans for a data center in Defiance, a city of 17,000 people surrounded by soybean fields in northwestern Ohio.
But people in the aptly named community are not taking any chances.
After learning the county’s economic development group had fielded inquiries from tech companies, residents spent months gathering signatures for a November 3 ballot measure to ban all but the smallest data centers. City officials announced a six-month moratorium on new project approvals.  
The fight in Defiance is part of a broader political backlash throughout Ohio — and across the nation — where mounting public anxiety about AI and cloud-computing infrastructure has transformed data center construction from an economic success story into a contentious midterm elections issue.
